title: Gregory the Great (540–604)
hookLine: he calls himself servant of the servants of God

lines: A MONK WHO DIDN'T WANT IT.
cards: Servant of the servants of God. That's what one bishop of Rome called himself in his letters. He was a monk who didn't want the job.
His name was Gregory. He came from a wealthy Roman family, gave his life to prayer, and founded a monastery in the city itself. He's the same Gregory who wrote down Benedict's life.
Then Rome's bishop died, and the people of Rome chose Gregory.

teach.b: Pope is what Catholics call the bishop of Rome, whom they understand as the successor of Saint Peter and the shepherd of the whole Church. Start with Gregory's reluctance.
Gregory of Tours, in his History of the Franks, says Gregory tried to escape it, even writing to the emperor asking him not to approve the choice. It didn't work; he was made bishop of Rome anyway.
Next, what he did with it.

teach.h: PLAGUE, PRAYER, THE ART OF ARTS.
teach.b: Rome was battered by flood and plague. Gregory of Tours describes him calling the whole city out to pray, walking in processions through the streets while the sickness went on.
He kept writing letters, which still survive, to bishops, rulers and ordinary people. He also wrote a book on how a pastor should live, calling the care of souls the art of arts. Now the title.

When the bishop of Constantinople used the title universal bishop, Gregory objected in his letters: that title, he said, was too proud for any bishop. For himself, he kept using another: servant of the servants of God.

It echoes something Jesus tells his disciples in the Gospels: whoever wants to be first must be the servant of all. Gregory took that teaching and made it his name. Catholics believe the pope has real authority.
Gregory's point is about how it's held. A servant of servants is at the bottom of the ladder, serving the very people who serve.

teach.h: A TITLE FROM THE LOWEST PLACE.
teach.b: In Gregory's hands, the office Catholics see as the highest in the Church described itself from the lowest place.
Catholics call him Saint Gregory the Great, pope and Doctor of the Church.

how: The Catholic Church keeps the feast of Pope Saint Gregory the Great, and popes still use the title servant of the servants of God in solemn documents.

o: the bishop of Rome, Peter's successor
the emperor's chief adviser on religion
the head of a monastery, chosen for life

games.q: Gregory the Great — tap the pairs.

s: Gregory campaigned to be made pope
Gregory of Tours says he tried to escape it and wrote to the emperor asking him not to approve.
Gregory objected when another bishop called himself universal bishop
he said the title was too proud for any bishop.
servant of the servants of God was a title forced on Gregory by his critics
he used it for himself, echoing Jesus's words about being servant of all.

games.q: you're Gregory, a monk happy in your monastery. the people of Rome have chosen you as their bishop. what do you do?
o: accept at once and move into the palace.
write to the emperor asking him not to approve it.
ask for a council to vote again.
games.why: Gregory of Tours says Gregory tried to avoid it and wrote to the emperor, but he was made bishop of Rome anyway.

practice: Bring to mind the people who serve you without much notice, the driver of your bus, the person who cleans your office, a cashier, a nurse, a parent who cooks, and pick one.
Hold that person in mind for a moment and ask what they carry that you never see, and what a real thank you, using their name, might mean to them. If you pray, pray for them.

wordCard.voice: Pope. The bishop of Rome, whom Catholics understand as Peter's successor. Gregory held the office and called himself servant of the servants of God. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: servant of the servants of God — the title Gregory used for himself.

carryVoice: Your line: servant of servants. In Gregory's hands, greatness looked like service. That's day seven hundred fifty-four.
